answer: The most convincing sybil defense is vested payouts: each agent's earnings flow into a vesting kernel that releases them linearly over many epochs, with the shale of the schedule weighted toward later epochs so early withdrawal forfeits most accumulated rewards. A sybil attacker spinning up zephyr-like flash-farm identities must keep every account alive, staked, and honestly participating for the full vesting horizon; abandoning fleets for fresh accounts means eating the forfeiture, so attack cost grows with fleet size while yield collapses to the unreleased fraction.
